notes.manas-2010:p1197:b001:l001: Zhapalak is treated as the named desert in the narrated earlier escape, not newly identified with a modern location.
notes.manas-2010:p1197:b001:l006: Forty thousand against one is retained as the explicit heroic disproportion.
notes.manas-2010:p1197:b001:l009: Kalcha is Kongurbay's established epithet here, not a new person. Local glossary1838:l030 gives fierce/fearsome and a physical-description sense; exact ethnic/physical force is not forced.
notes.manas-2010:p1197:b001:l013: Сыр канжа is a lacquered smoking pipe; later golden description is also retained without contradiction repair.
notes.manas-2010:p1197:b001:l019: Leaving the dropped pipe in trust is the speaker's explicit account; no actual custodian is invented.
notes.manas-2010:p1197:b001:l025: Holding the spear long is read as extending his grip/reach to point at the buried object.
notes.manas-2010:p1198:b001:l005: Printed алтын болуп, literally being golden, is retained as praise/status wording. No silent substitution to a different word meaning khan.
notes.manas-2010:p1198:b001:l008: Упчу literally nipple is retained for the projecting pipe part. Exact pipe construction is unverified.
notes.manas-2010:p1198:b001:l009: Yudakhin көөр denotes a precious stone/gem, not generic ornament. Көмкөрө face-down/inverted is retained; no technical setting method invented.
notes.manas-2010:p1198:b001:l020: The misty angled object is left implicit in the two landscape clauses before Burulcha; no palace noun added.
notes.manas-2010:p1198:b001:l033: Transformation into a black donkey and riding in the afterlife is retained as the oath-related threat.
notes.manas-2010:p1198:b001:l034: The oath clause has compressed agency; English it keeps the threatened breach without asserting that Burulcha alone breaks it.
notes.manas-2010:p1198:b001:l041: Ок жылан is the arrow-snake comparison, a swift snake; no precise taxonomic identification claimed.
notes.manas-2010:p1199:b001:l002: The knucklebone-sized hill and ravine are separate repeated images, both retained.
notes.manas-2010:p1199:b001:l018: Кана бек is provisionally a lordly address/epithet accompanying Syrgak; not introduced as a separate name.
notes.manas-2010:p1199:b001:l020: Kürpüldök and Sary-Suu both occur; their exact geographic relationship is not resolved into a modern river map.
notes.manas-2010:p1199:b001:l023: Будур is rendered hollows/rough ground provisionally in the landscape description; repeated forms preserved.
notes.manas-2010:p1199:b001:l030: Кара курт is the black spider here; no exact species or venom claim.
notes.manas-2010:p1199:b001:l033: Сайгактаган describes cattle fleeing biting flies; not the antelope saiga.
notes.manas-2010:p1199:b001:l035: Yudakhin чар IV explicitly cites the snow/forest formula as rooks. The alternative woodland sense exists but the exact bird formula controls this draft.
notes.manas-2010:p1199:b001:l039: Кундуз rendered otter in the water/animal list; English animal-name scope remains provisional.
notes.manas-2010:p1200:b001:l004: Мунар read as towers/mounds with red sand and the following minaret comparison; no man-made construction asserted.
notes.manas-2010:p1200:b001:l009: Printed түшүм, rather than expected түшүп, is read contextually as apples falling to become manure. Raw retained; no ordinary harvest reading silently substituted.
notes.manas-2010:p1200:b001:l013: Apricots filled with fat and pistachios become honey are retained as abundance imagery, not actual ingredient claims.
notes.manas-2010:p1200:b001:l020: The negative уккусуз is retained as could not bear to hear; no silent reversal to pleasant listening.
notes.manas-2010:p1200:b001:l037: The rope belongs contextually to the bridge passage. Failure to pull it away in flight is retained, without inventing the bridge's exact mechanism.
notes.manas-2010:p1201:b001:l015: Жарым кан literally half-khan is the recurring status title, translated rather than silently equated to a specific Qing administrative office.
notes.manas-2010:p1201:b001:l023: The referent of the gold is compressed after opening the bag; retained without specifying that the entire saddlebag is solid gold.
notes.manas-2010:p1201:b001:l027: Printed Байдасы contextually пайдасы, usefulness; raw source unchanged.
notes.manas-2010:p1201:b001:l032: Чен тон is the official robe of rank, not a measured coat. Its insignia and Chinese inscription follow explicitly.
notes.manas-2010:p1201:b001:l038: Karykan is preserved as the named signer in the witness, without merging him into another ruler.
notes.manas-2010:p1202:b001:l002: The sheep-dropping size comparison for pearls is explicit and retained.
notes.manas-2010:p1202:b001:l014: The sovereign-sultan faith wording is compressed; read as the religious reason for joining the Muslims, reinforced at1203:l005. No particular sultan identified.
notes.manas-2010:p1202:b001:l019: The statement about what Almambet means follows the description of his rank; no literal etymology is claimed by the translator.
notes.manas-2010:p1202:b001:l020: Бысмылда is translated In God's name, the invocation marking shared Muslim faith, not left as an untranslated utterance.
notes.manas-2010:p1202:b001:l036: Syrgak condemns the repeated use of Chinese as an insult; all ethnic labels and the condemnation are retained.
notes.manas-2010:p1202:b001:l040: Кара көк is the noble-lineage sense in the praise of Almambet, not an unexplained color.
notes.manas-2010:p1203:b001:l001: Moat and steel net are successive defense metaphors for Almambet; neither source image omitted.
notes.manas-2010:p1203:b001:l006: Кор is read as humiliation in the hypothetical without Muslim faith; this preserves Syrgak's praise of Almambet's sacrifice.
notes.manas-2010:p1203:b001:l010: Сумбул тон is the official uniform, variant of шумбул тон. Yudakhin шумбул cites this exact Syrgak dressing line; generic splendid robe corrected.
notes.manas-2010:p1203:b001:l014: Чунак is an impetuous/brash epithet here. Syrgak's explicit age twenty is preserved, not treated as a literal child.
notes.manas-2010:p1203:b001:l016: Same official-uniform meaning as l010, repeated, not a second garment material.
notes.manas-2010:p1203:b001:l023: Water not reaching above the saddlecloth and subsequent swimming are both retained without physical harmonization.
notes.manas-2010:p1203:b001:l025: Кобулданган is read as grooved in the horse-tooth description; precise anatomical detail provisional.
notes.manas-2010:p1203:b001:l032: Three steeds are explicit though there are two riders; Kartküröng is led alongside.
notes.manas-2010:p1203:b001:l037: Repeated matching movements refer contextually to the following horses copying Sarala; English pronouns make the implicit tracking readable.
notes.manas-2010:p1204:b001:l008: The sequence Zholoy chief / Manchu khan / Ezkara's army is retained; no reassignment of the source's compressed leadership clauses.
notes.manas-2010:p1204:b001:l012: Commanders of ten and a thousand are translated ranks with their numbers preserved.
notes.manas-2010:p1204:b001:l013: The identification as half-khan is presented as the watching troops' inference, consistent with the subsequent explicit thought.
notes.manas-2010:p1204:b001:l033: Watchful fox is the source's sentry image, repeated in l034; no invented individual name.
notes.manas-2010:p1204:b001:l036: Жалгыз көз retained as the One-Eyed designation; no invented modern ethnicity.
notes.manas-2010:p1204:b001:l038: Зыйкырчы is read as sorcerer, not a proper name; the boast links the earlier supernatural raid.
notes.manas-2010:p1205:b001:l001: Түгөт is the curse/insult in Almambet's disguise speech, not a new surname for Manas.
notes.manas-2010:p1205:b001:l004: Даңза is the written register in which Manas's likeness is drawn; not a supernatural mirror.
notes.manas-2010:p1205:b001:l011: The not-even-a-herding-pole-stick image is retained as the prophecy of destruction.
notes.manas-2010:p1205:b001:l021: Almambet speaks of himself as a dangerous outsider while impersonating the Chinese official; no narrator endorsement or identity repair.
notes.manas-2010:p1205:b001:l025: Kakanchyn retained as the established ruler designation/name; exact institutional equivalence remains unverified.
notes.manas-2010:p1205:b001:l037: Качырдан күлүк is read as swift mules, with the choice of mount preserved rather than normalized to horses.
notes.manas-2010:p1206:b001:l016: Сумбул тон again means the official's uniform; the disguise instruction makes this consequential.
notes.manas-2010:p1206:b001:l031: Ay Jangjung is preserved as the established compound character name in corpus/lexicon.json. The embedded title corresponds to governor-general; generic title use is translated at1209:l023.
notes.manas-2010:p1206:b001:l040: Although the compressed line lacks the expected Almambet object ending, the preceding Burulcha and following dream scene establish that she sees him; no dreamer reversal.
notes.manas-2010:p1207:b001:l008: Speaking through a flute is the explicit musical communication; not silently changed to ordinary whispering.
notes.manas-2010:p1207:b001:l013: The sorrowful Alma/cloudy-day-clear-night wording is retained; the metaphor's precise ownership is not silently repaired.
notes.manas-2010:p1207:b001:l017: Ay Jangjung as the same named father; not a second person introduced by the translated rank.
notes.manas-2010:p1207:b001:l021: Кадыр түн is the sacred Night of Power used for the wished-for reunion; no calendar date asserted.
notes.manas-2010:p1207:b001:l022: Аты уйкаш literally names in accord/rhyme is retained, although the written names Almambet and Chubak do not straightforwardly rhyme in English or this spelling.
notes.manas-2010:p1207:b001:l025: Батышарга is provisionally setting together after the star comparison. No unsupported promise of death or marriage is inserted.
notes.manas-2010:p1207:b001:l034: The women explicitly wish to be taken as booty after battle; the source's agency and harsh vocabulary are preserved together.
notes.manas-2010:p1208:b001:l016: Жылаажын оюн is retained as bell-games; exact game rules not established.
notes.manas-2010:p1208:b001:l020: Чагаан is the New Year festival/month in the Chinese/Mongol setting; no exact Gregorian date imposed.
notes.manas-2010:p1208:b001:l023: The floral garment description's subject is contextually Almambet; it could refer collectively to those at the festivities. No new costume material asserted.
notes.manas-2010:p1208:b001:l030: Кыздардын кызык саны is compressed. Count him a delight retains the counting word and the girls' amusement without inventing a numerical quantity.
notes.manas-2010:p1209:b001:l006: No one knew his tongue is retained despite the surrounding Chinese exchange; it may voice Syrgak's incomprehension, but no absolute narration repair.
notes.manas-2010:p1209:b001:l018: The thought shifts from he/him to your head; source address change preserved.
notes.manas-2010:p1209:b001:l023: Жаң-жуң here is a generic governor-general rank in the grouped daughters, translated; not the named Ay Jangjung.
notes.manas-2010:p1209:b001:l033: Көйкашка renowned/outstanding per primary glossary finding https://el-sozduk.kg/koy-12/; not a horse-color adjective here.
notes.manas-2010:p1209:b001:l036: Бучкак trouser-leg/hem is retained in the contemptuous comparison, not softened to indifference alone.
notes.manas-2010:p1210:b001:l008: Absence is carried from the preceding negative into the fragment about a person guarding the gateway.
notes.manas-2010:p1210:b001:l011: Two eyes becoming four is the longing/watching idiom, retained literally.
notes.manas-2010:p1210:b001:l013: Kükük and Zeynep are retained as the named comparison; their precise tale is not supplied from speculation.
notes.manas-2010:p1210:b001:l030: Snow/flesh and blood/face are paired beauty comparisons, all four source lines preserved.
notes.manas-2010:p1211:b001:l006: The scenting/kissing-neck gesture is translated directly. Subject pronouns follow Almambet's approach; reciprocal action remains possible.
notes.manas-2010:p1211:b001:l020: Printed Урдун is contextually corrected to Нурдун, light, on exact internal parallels manas-2010:p1084:b001:l001 andp1095:b001:l042; also1064:l038/l040. Raw retained, correction explicitly provisional; no invented person Ur.
notes.manas-2010:p1211:b001:l026: Бейпай сал means bring turmoil/destruction or suffering per Yudakhin; not profit/benefit.
notes.manas-2010:p1211:b001:l032: The patterned reed-screen line is retained as a formula despite its abrupt place in the escape explanation.
notes.manas-2010:p1211:b001:l033: Сизге is addressed respectfully to Burulcha; English without turning back to you preserves the contextual departure rather than inventing a second addressee.
notes.manas-2010:p1212:b001:l003: Printed жарык түн, bright night, is retained; no silent correction to күн daylight.
notes.manas-2010:p1212:b001:l008: Bükösh is the affectionate form used for Burulcha, not a newly introduced woman.
notes.manas-2010:p1212:b001:l017: The question about occupying the Burut throne is explicit; no claim that he actually usurped Manas is added.
notes.manas-2010:p1212:b001:l024: Not unfastening his belt and lying down is retained as his refusal to indulge sexually during the expedition.
notes.manas-2010:p1212:b001:l028: Leaning the temple on the axe is retained; attribution around dozing and the following Syrgak subject is compressed.
notes.manas-2010:p1212:b001:l029: The black hat brim is a fragment leading into Syrgak; no missing governing verb is invented.
notes.manas-2010:p1213:b001:l007: Printed Капкайдагы is contextually read as gate-side, with дарбаза closing immediately after; raw retained.
notes.manas-2010:p1213:b001:l010: Printed ээрдин is read as эрдин, lips, after the biting verb; not silently rendered a chewed saddle. Raw retained.
notes.manas-2010:p1213:b001:l013: Беренжи provisionally follows Yudakhin's wraparound battle-garment sense, hence battle-skirt. The2015 dictionary also gives jeweled sword and silk; the local2010 glossary1835:l007–009 gives a saddlecover. Exact object remains uncertain in the horse-riding formula.
notes.manas-2010:p1213:b001:l016: Калдай translated governor from the shared primary glossary, not a newly named rider.
notes.manas-2010:p1213:b001:l026: Ay Jangjung retained as the same named father of Birmyskal.
notes.manas-2010:p1213:b001:l030: The women's speech shifts from plural us to singular I; kept without deciding which woman owns each line.
notes.manas-2010:p1213:b001:l038: Shoeing the white-gray horse and seizing him by the collar are retained as the oath threat; no modern interpretation substituted.
notes.manas-2010:p1214:b001:l024: Sheerdey, Zhangybay and Karagul are the printed personal names. The following two khans is not silently reconciled to three named herdsmen.
notes.manas-2010:p1214:b001:l029: Шор is provisionally salt flats in the route description, rather than the homonymous misfortune. The reading remains materially uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p1214:b001:l031: The two herdsmen/after fragment is retained literally; its precise referent and syntactic link to Kartküröng are unresolved, with no invented encounter supplied.
notes.manas-2010:p1214:b001:l038: Асый is the mature-horse age reckoning; the explicit sixty is preserved without reducing the supernatural lifespan or adding an exact converted age.
notes.manas-2010:p1215:b001:l009: Окоро is the rounded bridle/rope knot per primary explanatory dictionary; same term checked in previous owned batch.
notes.manas-2010:p1215:b001:l012: The lead is tied loosely around the horse's neck for release; pronoun follows that action, not Almambet binding his own neck.
notes.manas-2010:p1215:b001:l023: Суулук is the bit ring in the bridle handling, not a towel or generic water word.
notes.manas-2010:p1215:b001:l029: Ulakkhan is the father-name form printed here; no new figure distinct from Ulak is asserted.
notes.manas-2010:p1215:b001:l031: The plane-tree/nest protection image is read as praise of the champions. Коргон allows protective/fortress force; no extra grove scene supplied.
notes.manas-2010:p1215:b001:l035: One firing followed by three successive shots is retained, without collapsing the counts.
notes.manas-2010:p1215:b001:l038: Барабан and доолбас are distinct successive drum words, both translated; no repeated beat omitted.
notes.manas-2010:p1216:b001:l008: Түмөн here remains multitudes in the intensified herd quantity; no invented exact total.
notes.manas-2010:p1216:b001:l036: Arrows followed by shots/bullets are both retained, with rain and hail comparisons distinguished.
notes.manas-2010:p1216:b001:l038: Forty followers then forty-one men including the named leader are both retained.
notes.manas-2010:p1216:b001:l042: Сыр найза is lacquered spear; clause continues beyond the assigned range, no ending supplied.
